context.exploration_scope: Applied E45's Trigger-first pattern to Studio Intelligence: compared current real state against the E40 PB baseline and S11's per-goal classification baseline, reusing both as-is

problem: S11 established that Studio Intelligence correctly finds nothing to execute right now, but that alone does not establish an operating discipline for WHEN to check again -- without a Trigger-first check, every future phase would have to redo the full S1..S11 pipeline regardless of whether anything actually changed.

decision.decision_summary: Compared current state against E40's fixed baseline (goals/capabilities/trace/priority/currency) and S11's per-goal classification baseline: 0 changes detected. NO_STATE_CHANGE -- downstream Decision pipeline not exercised. 0 existing DEFERRED/RESOLVED verdicts force-changed, 0 automatic execution. Verdict: NO_STATE_CHANGE.

action.action_summary: Re-derived current Goal/Capability/Trace/Priority state and each production goal's Decision/Boundary classification fresh; compared against the existing E40 and S11 baselines (reused, not re-derived); generated at most 1 candidate only if real change was found.

result.note: No real change since S10/S11 -- correctly stopped at NO_STATE_CHANGE rather than re-running the full Decision pipeline for no reason.

cause.root_cause_summary: Without an explicit Trigger-first check, an operational system either re-verifies everything on every run (wasteful) or silently assumes nothing changed (risky) -- reusing the exact E45 pattern for Studio Intelligence closes that gap the same way it was closed for Project Evolution.

lesson: The same Trigger-first discipline that made Project Evolution's operational loop (E45..E51) sustainable applies directly to Studio Intelligence's decision loop: check for real change first, and only pay the cost of the full Decision pipeline when there is something real to react to.
